analysis: Examined docs/reports/README.md base and head: the only changes are the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and one new index link at head line 7 to 2026-10-31-public-cluster-models.md. This is documentation only, with no security controls changed. The linked document's existence and content were not supplied, so its claims about public cluster model declarations are unverified. Examined the added Swift file provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Config/ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release.swift only through the bounded patch excerpt, which is truncated; no full text unit was supplied. The visible portion defines ReleaseModel (runtime_model_id, artifact_sha256) and releaseModels/qualifiedModels. It builds the release's cluster_runtime model list from bundled ClusterPairServingGrants.records, keeping only records that are isConsistent, have outcome .passed and have a stage adapter, then dedupes and sorts them. Nothing visible bypasses a control. The security-relevant open questions are outside the visible text. (1) How the coordinator or platform consumes these release-registered cluster_runtime facts and whether it treats them as authorization. The facts are self-computed by the release's own CLI and worker, so they are not independent attestation and must not feed TB-011/TB-002 serving authorization or substitute for qualification (T-052, T-054, T-056). (2) The truncated remainder of the file, including how the facts are assembled, signed or transmitted, and the pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. (3) Cluster/pipeline-parallel traffic is not covered by the current threat model, which is a potential model gap for a follow-up. No regression is identified from the visible evidence, but coverage of the new Swift file is incomplete, so deeper review is recommended.
